Utility Conditions: To the best of the Utilities Department’s knowledge, there does not appear to be any on-site City of Sarasota utilities in conflict with the proposed improvements. Approved with conditions: 1. The existing water meter/s cannot be removed, and curb stops cannot be turned off before the Utilities Billing Office is contacted. The Utilities Billing Office is located at 1575 2nd Street Sarasota, FL 34236 with hours of operation from 8:00 A.M. to 4:30 P.M. Monday – Friday (excluding holidays and emergencies). Utilities Billing Office staff can be reached by calling 941-263-6260. 2. If the existing water meter is used as a construction/demo meter, a Reduced Pressure (RP) Backflow preventer must be installed prior to demolition and construction. A building inspector shall inspect the backflow and the backflow hanging tag. 3. If a backflow is installed, the property owner is required to provide a (RP) Backflow report/certification. The backflow test report shall be emailed to Backflow.utilities@sarasotafl.gov. 4. If a backflow is required and a backflow is not installed and a certificate (test report) is not provided, the Utilities Department will turn off the water. Billing Office fees will apply. 5. If water from the fire hydrant is used, an appropriate fee shall be paid directly to the Utilities Billing Office. 6. Call 811 for locates prior to beginning demolition. 7. The location of the existing wastewater lateral (sewer service line) shall be capped at the property line prior to demolition. The painted green wood stake shall be placed next to the capped pipe. 8. Be advised that any Contractor that damages any portion of the City’s potable water, wastewater, and/or reclaimed water infrastructure shall be totally financially responsible for the repair of any such damaged infrastructure. All Contractors proposing to work directly on or near any portion of the City’s potable water, wastewater, and/or reclaimed water infrastructure shall have the appropriate repair materials (pipe, fittings, etc.), tools, and qualified staff available onsite to perform immediate repairs should damage to such infrastructure occur.

Description of Work.Conditions: Utility Conditions: To the best of the Utilities Department’s knowledge, there does not appear to be any on-site City of Sarasota utilities in conflict with the proposed improvements. Approved with conditions: 1. The existing water meter/s cannot be removed, and curb stops cannot be turned off before the Utilities Billing Office is contacted. The Utilities Billing Office is located at 1575 2nd Street Sarasota, FL 34236 with hours of operation from 8:00 A.M. to 4:30 P.M. Monday – Friday (excluding holidays and emergencies). Utilities Billing Office staff can be reached by calling 941-263-6260. 2. If the existing water meter is used as a construction/demo meter, a Reduced Pressure (RP) Backflow preventer must be installed prior to demolition and construction. A building inspector shall inspect the backflow and the backflow hanging tag. 3. If a backflow is installed, the property owner is required to provide a (RP) Backflow report/certification. The backflow test report shall be emailed to Backflow.utilities@sarasotafl.gov. 4. If a backflow is required and a backflow is not installed and a certificate (test report) is not provided, the Utilities Department will turn off the water. Billing Office fees will apply. 5. If water from the fire hydrant is used, an appropriate fee shall be paid directly to the Utilities Billing Office. 6. Call 811 for locates prior to beginning demolition. 7. The location of the existing wastewater lateral (sewer service line) shall be capped at the property line prior to demolition. The painted green wood stake shall be placed next to the capped pipe. Be advised that any Contractor that damages any portion of the City’s potable water, wastewater, and/or reclaimed water infrastructure shall be totally financially responsible for the repair of any such damaged infrastructure. All Contractors who propose to work directly on or in close proximity of any portion of the City’s potable water, wastewater, and/or reclaimed water infrastructure shall have the appropriate repair materials (pipe, fittings, etc.), tools, and qualified staff available onsite to perform immediate repairs should damage to such infrastructure occur. Arborist Conditions: (**TREE PROTECTION CONDITION** ARBORIST CONDITIONS **) Tree protection barriers are to be installed prior to construction and remain until Final Landscaping of property begins. Section VII-312. (a)(f) The owner, builder, contractor and all other persons involved with the construction of the home shall be responsible for the oversight of tree protection during the construction of home. IF THE FENCING MUST BE MOVED OR REMOVED FOR ACCESS ISSUES, THE CITY ARBORIST MUST BE CONTACTED FIRST. A 3-6" layer of mulch with plywood on top must be added before the fencing can be removed. Failure to properly maintain tree protection will result in an automatic $250.00 citation, with potential additional daily fines for continued non-compliance. Distance from tree trunk to tree protection must be at least 10 feet, or as hardscape allows. In some cases, an area of 10ft around tree to have 3”-6” layer of mulch with plywood covering. Maintained throughout construction activities. Arecas and Pygmy date palms are excluded from this. Sec. VII-312 (c) Any excess soil, additional fill, vehicles, equipment, liquid waste, solvents or construction debris shall not be placed during construction within the protective barrier area surrounding a tree. The tree or its root system surrounded by a protective barrier shall not be otherwise damaged. (TREE PROTECTION DETAILS) Grand trees, Live and Sand Live oaks 24" DBH and over and Slash, and Longleaf pines plus Red Cedar tree 20" DBH and over require: 20ft A: Chain link fencing B: Chain link shall be minimum of 6 feet in height. C: Tree protection barricades shall be installed a minimum of 20 feet radius around the tree D: In some cases, an area of 20ft around tree trunk to have 3”-6” layer of mulch with plywood covering. This must be approved by City Arborist, and maintained throughout construction activities. Tree protection for all other trees & palms, aka Non-grand trees require: 10ft A: Vertical wood members must be a minimum of 2” x 2” B: Vertical wood members must be a minimum of 3 feet from finished grade C: Vertical wood members may not exceed a distance greater than 8 feet D: Top wooden rails must be a minimum of 1” deep by 4” wide E: Distance from tree trunk to tree protection must be at least 10 feet, or as hardscape allows. F: In some cases, an area of 10ft around tree to have 3”-6” layer of mulch with plywood covering. Maintained throughout construction activities. Tree protection barriers are to be installed prior to construction and remain until final landscaping begins. City Arborist MUST BE NOTIFIED, and any modifications APPROVED PRIOR TO THE MODIFICATION OF TREE PROTECTION BARRIERS. 941-263-6492 Sec VII-312(e)(3) Root pruning must be performed prior to any construction activities and inspected by the City Arborist before requesting building permit inspections. Per Sec. VII-331.-Protection of tree roots. No tree root larger than three (3”) inches in diameter shall be severed unless a Root Management Plan by a certified arborist and/or landscape architect has been submitted and approved by the city arborist. Root pruning must be performed prior to any construction activities and inspected by the City Arborist before requesting building permit inspections. (1) All roots must be severed clean at the protected root zone of protected and grand trees to prevent root damage. (2) Root pruning must be performed with an approved cutting type of equipment, such as a chainsaw, hand saw or other cutting equipment. (3) Root pruning must be performed prior to any construction activities and inspected by the city arborist before requesting building permit inspections.

Utilities Billing Office staff can be reached by calling 941-263-6260. 2. If the existing water meter is used as a construction/demo meter, a Reduced Pressure (RP) Backflow preventer must be installed prior to demolition and construction. A building inspector shall inspect the backflow and the backflow hanging tag. 3. If a backflow is installed, the property owner is required to provide a (RP) Backflow report/certification. The backflow test report shall be emailed to Backflow.utilities@sarasotafl.gov. 4. If a backflow is required and a backflow is not installed and a certificate (test report) is not provided, the Utilities Department will turn off the water. Billing Office fees will apply. 5. If water from the fire hydrant is used, an appropriate fee shall be paid directly to the Utilities Billing Office. 6. Call 811 for locates prior to beginning demolition. 7. The location of the existing wastewater lateral (sewer service line) shall be capped at the property line prior to demolition. The painted green wood stake shall be placed next to the capped pipe. 8. Description of Work.Conditions: Building Conditions: Prior to Plumbing final inspection you must: • 1- Have an approved Erosion/Siltation inspection. • 2- Stub up domestic water service and install backflow preventor. • 3- Stub up and cap sewer. • 4- Send Backflow Certification to the Utilities department: Backflow.Utilities@sarasotafl.gov or fax 941.365.4840 • 5- Initial erosion, tree barrier and plumbing final before must be approved prior to demolition of structure. • 6- Tree Protection Barriers must be installed at initial erosion inspection and erosion controls and tree barriers must be maintained throughout Construction. • 7- If you have any questions about tree protection barriers, contact City Arborist Jackie Hartley @ 263-6536. Utility Conditions: To the best of the Utilities Department’s knowledge, there does not appear to be any on-site City of Sarasota utilities in conflict with the proposed improvements. Approved with conditions: 1. The existing water meter/s cannot be removed, and curb stops cannot be turned off before the Utilities Billing Office is contacted. The Utilities Billing Office is located at 1575 2nd Street Sarasota, FL 34236 with hours of operation from 8:00 A.M. to 4:30 P.M. Monday – Friday (excluding holidays and emergencies). Utilities Billing Office staff can be reached by calling 941-263-6260. 2. If the existing water meter is used as a construction/demo meter, a Reduced Pressure (RP) Backflow preventer must be installed prior to demolition and construction. A building inspector shall inspect the backflow and the backflow hanging tag. 3. If a backflow is installed, the property owner is required to provide a (RP) Backflow report/certification. The backflow test report shall be emailed to Backflow.utilities@sarasotafl.gov. 4. If a backflow is required and a backflow is not installed and a certificate (test report) is not provided, the Utilities Department will turn off the water. Billing Office fees will apply. 5. If water from the fire hydrant is used, an appropriate fee shall be paid directly to the Utilities Billing Office. 6. Call 811 for locates prior to beginning demolition. 7. The location of the existing wastewater lateral (sewer service line) shall be capped at the property line prior to demolition. The painted green wood stake shall be placed next to the capped pipe. 8. Be advised that any Contractor that damages any portion of the City’s potable water, wastewater, and/or reclaimed water infrastructure shall be totally financially responsible for the repair of any such damaged infrastructure. All Contractors proposing to work directly on or near any portion of the City’s potable water, wastewater, and/or reclaimed water infrastructure shall have the appropriate repair materials (pipe, fittings, etc.), tools, and qualified staff available onsite to perform immediate repairs should damage to such infrastructure occur.

Per Sec VII-312(e) Fences and walls shall not be installed where they interfere with the root system of existing trees. Post holes and trenches shall be adjusted to avoid damage to major roots. Footings for walls shall end at the point where large roots (over three inches in diameter) are encountered. Post holes and trenches located close to trees shall be adjusted to avoid damage to major roots. Per Sec. VII-331.-Protection of tree roots. No tree root larger than three (3”) inches in diameter shall be severed unless a Root Management Plan by a certified arborist and/or landscape architect has been submitted and approved by the city arborist. Zoning Conditions: Fence posts/column locations shall be adjusted as to not damage root system of trees. Roots 3" or greater shall not be cut or severed. No trees are to be removed or relocated. Description of Work.Conditions: Building Conditions: Prior to Plumbing final inspection you must: • 1- Have an approved Erosion/Siltation inspection. • 2- Stub up domestic water service and install backflow preventor. • 3- Stub up and cap sewer. • 4- Send Backflow Certification to the Utilities department: Backflow.Utilities@sarasotafl.gov or fax 941.365.4840 • 5- Initial erosion, tree barrier and plumbing final before must be approved prior to demolition of structure. • 6- Tree Protection Barriers must be installed at initial erosion inspection and erosion controls and tree barriers must be maintained throughout Construction. • 7- If you have any questions about tree protection barriers, contact City Arborist Jackie Hartley @ 263-6536. Utility Conditions: To the best of the Utilities Department’s knowledge, there does not appear to be any on-site City of Sarasota utilities in conflict with the proposed improvements. Approved with conditions: 1. The existing water meter/s cannot be removed, and curb stops cannot be turned off before the Utilities Billing Office is contacted. The Utilities Billing Office is located at 1575 2nd Street Sarasota, FL 34236 with hours of operation from 8:00 A.M. to 4:30 P.M. Monday – Friday (excluding holidays and emergencies). Utilities Billing Office staff can be reached by calling 941-263-6260. 2. If the existing water meter is used as a construction/demo meter, a Reduced Pressure (RP) Backflow preventer must be installed prior to demolition and construction. A building inspector shall inspect the backflow and the backflow hanging tag. 3. If a backflow is installed, the property owner is required to provide a (RP) Backflow report/certification. The backflow test report shall be emailed to Backflow.utilities@sarasotafl.gov. 4. If a backflow is required and a backflow is not installed and a certificate (test report) is not provided, the Utilities Department will turn off the water. Billing Office fees will apply. 5. If water from the fire hydrant is used, an appropriate fee shall be paid directly to the Utilities Billing Office. 6. Call 811 for locates prior to beginning demolition. 7. The location of the existing wastewater lateral (sewer service line) shall be capped at the property line prior to demolition. The painted green wood stake shall be placed next to the capped pipe. Be advised that any Contractor that damages any portion of the City’s potable water, wastewater, and/or reclaimed water infrastructure shall be totally financially responsible for the repair of any such damaged infrastructure. All Contractors who propose to work directly on or in close proximity of any portion of the City’s potable water, wastewater, and/or reclaimed water infrastructure shall have the appropriate repair materials (pipe, fittings, etc.), tools, and qualified staff available onsite to perform immediate repairs should damage to such infrastructure occur. Arborist Conditions: Tree protection barriers shall be installed prior to the commencement of construction and shall remain in place until final building inspection. The City Arborist shall be notified prior to installation, and any modifications to tree protection barriers must be reviewed and approved by the City Arborist before changes are made. Section VII-312. (a)(f) The owner, builder, superintendent, contractor and site employees shall be responsible for the oversite of tree protection during all construction. A: Chain link must be used for grand tree protection B: Chain link shall be minimum of 6 feet in height. C: Tree protection barricades shall be installed a minimum of 20 feet radius around the tree. A Grand Tree, as defined in the City of Sarasota Zoning Code Article II, Division 2, Sec. II-201 Tree protection related definitions is a “Live Oak (Quercus Virginiana) or similar nomenclature for species, consisting of a tree and its root system whose single trunk or combined trunk DBH size is 24” (addition of all trunk DBH for a multi trunk tree) or greater”. For more information on tree protection, please see City of Sarasota Zoning Code, Section VII-312 Protection of trees during development, viewable online at www.Municode.com/Library/Fl/Sarasota/Codes/Zoning https://www.sarasotafl.gov/home/showdocument?id=10704 A: Vertical wood members must be a minimum of 2” x 2” B: Vertical wood members must be a minimum of 3 feet from finished grade C: Vertical wood members may not exceed a distance greater than 8 feet D: Top wooden rails must be a minimum of 1” deep by 4” wide E: Distance from tree trunk to tree protection must be at least 10 feet For more information on tree protection, please see City of Sarasota Zoning Code, Section VII-312 Protection of trees during development, viewable online at www.Municode.com/Library/Fl/Sarasota/Codes/Zoning https://www.sarasotafl.gov/home/showdocument?id=10706

Description of Work.Conditions: Building Conditions: Prior to Plumbing final inspection you must: • 1- Have an approved Erosion/Siltation inspection. • 2- Stub up domestic water service and install backflow preventor. • 3- Stub up and cap sewer. • 4- Send Backflow Certification to the Utilities department: Backflow.Utilities@sarasotafl.gov or fax 941.365.4840 • 5- Initial erosion, tree barrier and plumbing final before must be approved prior to demolition of structure. • 6- Tree Protection Barriers must be installed at initial erosion inspection and erosion controls and tree barriers must be maintained throughout Construction. • 7- If you have any questions about tree protection barriers, contact City Arborist Jackie Hartley @ 263-6536. Arborist Conditions: Tree protection barriers are to be installed prior to construction and remain until building final. City Arborist must be notified, and any modifications approved prior to the modification of tree protection barriers. Any root pruning must be performed prior to any construction activities and inspected by the City Arborist before requesting building permit inspections. Grand trees, Live and Sand Live oaks 24" DBH and over and Slash, and Longleaf pines plus Red Cedar tree 20" DBH and over required, A: Chain link fencing B: Chain link shall be minimum of 6 feet in height. C: Tree protection barricades shall be installed a minimum of 20 feet radius around the tree Tree protection for non-grand trees require, A: Vertical wood members must be a minimum of 2” x 2” B: Vertical wood members must be a minimum of 3 feet from finished grade C: Vertical wood members may not exceed a distance greater than 8 feet D: Top wooden rails must be a minimum of 1” deep by 4” wide E: Distance from tree trunk to tree protection must be at least 10 feet Section VII-312. (a)(f) The owner, builder, superintendent, contractor and site employees shall be responsible for the oversite of tree protection during all construction. Any required root pruning must be approved and inspected by the City Arborist. Any required branch pruning must be completed by an ISA certified arborist. Utility Conditions: 1. City of Sarasota Utilities Department (COSUD) conditions: a. The existing water meter(s) cannot be removed, and curb stops cannot be turned off without first contacting the Utilities Billing Office. The Utilities Billing Office is located at 1575 2nd Street. Office hours are 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and they can be reached at 941-263-6260. b. If the existing water meter is to be used as a construction/demo meter, the property owner must provide a Backflow (RP) report/certification. The backflow test report shall be faxed to the Utilities Department at (941) 365-4840 (Attn: Dawn McCall) or emailed to Backflow.Utilities@sarasotafl.gov. c. If the existing water meter is not used as a construction/demo meter, the water and fire service lines must be capped at the property line during demolition. After the Building Permit and Utilities Construction Permit are approved, the developer must cap them at the main and remove them in accordance with the City’s Engineering Design Criteria Manual (EDCM). d. A building inspector shall inspect the backflow and verify the hanging tag as proof of the required backflow certification. e. If a backflow device is not installed and a certificate (test report) is not provided, the Utilities Department will turn off the water. Billing Office fees will apply. f. If water from a fire hydrant is to be used, the appropriate fee shall be paid directly to the Utilities Billing Office. g. The existing wastewater lateral (sanitary sewer service line) must be capped at the property line during demolition. A painted green wood stake shall be placed next to the capped pipe. h. The applicant shall contact the Utilities Department and Public Works – Engineering Division prior to starting any work near City utilities located in the right-of-way. Contact information is available on the City of Sarasota website: https://www.sarasotafl.gov/Home.

Description of Work.Conditions: Building Conditions: Prior to Plumbing final inspection you must: • 1- Have an approved Erosion/Siltation inspection. • 2- Stub up domestic water service and install backflow preventor. • 3- Stub up and cap sewer. • 4- Send Backflow Certification to the Utilities department: Backflow.Utilities@sarasotafl.gov or fax 941.365.4840 • 5- Initial erosion, tree barrier and plumbing final before must be approved prior to demolition of structure. • 6- Tree Protection Barriers must be installed at initial erosion inspection and erosion controls and tree barriers must be maintained throughout Construction. • 7- If you have any questions about tree protection barriers, contact City Arborist Jackie Hartley @ 263-6536. Utility Conditions: To the best of the Utilities Department’s knowledge, there does not appear to be any on-site City of Sarasota utilities in conflict with the proposed improvements. Approved with conditions: 1. The existing water meter/s cannot be removed, and curb stops cannot be turned off before the Utilities Billing Office is contacted. The Utilities Billing Office is located at 1575 2nd Street Sarasota, FL 34236 with hours of operation from 8:00 A.M. to 4:30 P.M. Monday – Friday (excluding holidays and emergencies). Utilities Billing Office staff can be reached by calling 941-263-6260. 2. If the existing water meter is used as a construction/demo meter, a Reduced Pressure (RP) Backflow preventer must be installed prior to demolition and construction. A building inspector shall inspect the backflow and the backflow hanging tag. 3. If a backflow is installed, the property owner is required to provide a (RP) Backflow report/certification. The backflow test report shall be emailed to Backflow.utilities@sarasotafl.gov. 4. If a backflow is required and a backflow is not installed and a certificate (test report) is not provided, the Utilities Department will turn off the water. Billing Office fees will apply. 5. If water from the fire hydrant is used, an appropriate fee shall be paid directly to the Utilities Billing Office. 6. Call 811 for locates prior to beginning demolition. 7. The location of the existing wastewater lateral (sewer service line) shall be capped at the property line prior to demolition. The painted green wood stake shall be placed next to the capped pipe. Be advised that any Contractor that damages any portion of the City’s potable water, wastewater, and/or reclaimed water infrastructure shall be totally financially responsible for the repair of any such damaged infrastructure. All Contractors who propose to work directly on or in close proximity of any portion of the City’s potable water, wastewater, and/or reclaimed water infrastructure shall have the appropriate repair materials (pipe, fittings, etc.), tools, and qualified staff available onsite to perform immediate repairs should damage to such infrastructure occur. Arborist Conditions: Tree protection barriers shall be installed prior to the commencement of construction and shall remain in place until final building inspection. The City Arborist shall be notified prior to installation, and any modifications to tree protection barriers must be reviewed and approved by the City Arborist before changes are made. Section VII-312. (a)(f) The owner, builder, superintendent, contractor and site employees shall be responsible for the oversite of tree protection during all construction. A: Vertical wood members must be a minimum of 2” x 2” B: Vertical wood members must be a minimum of 3 feet from finished grade C: Vertical wood members may not exceed a distance greater than 8 feet D: Top wooden rails must be a minimum of 1” deep by 4” wide E: Distance from tree trunk to tree protection must be at least 10 feet For more information on tree protection, please see City of Sarasota Zoning Code, Section VII-312 Protection of trees during development, viewable online at www.Municode.com/Library/Fl/Sarasota/Codes/Zoning https://www.sarasotafl.gov/home/showdocument?id=10706A: Chain link must be used for grand tree protection B: Chain link shall be minimum of 6 feet in height. C: Tree protection barricades shall be installed a minimum of 20 feet radius around the tree. A Grand Tree, as defined in the City of Sarasota Zoning Code Article II, Division 2, Sec. II-201 Tree protection related definitions is a “Live Oak (Quercus Virginiana) or similar nomenclature for species, consisting of a tree and its root system whose single trunk or combined trunk DBH size is 24” (addition of all trunk DBH for a multi trunk tree) or greater”. For more information on tree protection, please see City of Sarasota Zoning Code, Section VII-312 Protection of trees during development, viewable online at www.Municode.com/Library/Fl/Sarasota/Codes/Zoning https://www.sarasotafl.gov/home/showdocument?id=10704

Description of Work.Conditions: Arborist Conditions: (TREE PROTECTION DETAILS) *1 Grand tree- Slash Pine on adjacent property must be protected* Grand trees, Live and Sand Live oaks 24" DBH and over and Slash, and Longleaf pines plus Red Cedar tree 20" DBH and over require: 20ft A: Chain link fencing B: Chain link shall be minimum of 6 feet in height. C: Tree protection barricades shall be installed a minimum of 20 feet radius around the tree D: In some cases, an area of 20ft around tree trunk to have 3”-6” layer of mulch with plywood covering. This must be approved by City Arborist, and maintained throughout construction activities. Tree protection for all other trees & palms, aka Non-grand trees require: 10ft A: Vertical wood members must be a minimum of 2” x 2” B: Vertical wood members must be a minimum of 3 feet from finished grade C: Vertical wood members may not exceed a distance greater than 8 feet D: Top wooden rails must be a minimum of 1” deep by 4” wide E: Distance from tree trunk to tree protection must be at least 10 feet, or as hardscape allows. F: In some cases, an area of 10ft around tree to have 3”-6” layer of mulch with plywood covering. Maintained throughout construction activities. Tree protection barriers are to be installed prior to construction and remain until final landscaping begins. City Arborist MUST BE NOTIFIED, and any modifications APPROVED PRIOR TO THE MODIFICATION OF TREE PROTECTION BARRIERS. 941-263-6492Sec VII-312(e)(3) Root pruning must be performed prior to any construction activities and inspected by the City Arborist before requesting building permit inspections. (FILL & DEBRIS IN TPZ) Sec. VII-312 (c) Any excess soil, additional fill, vehicles, equipment, liquid waste, solvents or construction debris shall not be placed during construction within the protective barrier area surrounding a tree. Description of Work.Conditions: Building Conditions: Prior to Plumbing final inspection you must: • 1- Have an approved Erosion/Siltation inspection. • 2- Stub up domestic water service and install backflow preventor. • 3- Stub up and cap sewer. • 4- Send Backflow Certification to the Utilities department: Backflow.Utilities@sarasotafl.gov or fax 941.365.4840 • 5- Initial erosion, tree barrier and plumbing final before must be approved prior to demolition of structure. • 6- Tree Protection Barriers must be installed at initial erosion inspection and erosion controls and tree barriers must be maintained throughout Construction. • 7- If you have any questions about tree protection barriers, contact City Arborist Jackie Hartley @ 263-6536. Utility Conditions: To the best of the Utilities Department’s knowledge, there does not appear to be any on-site City of Sarasota utilities in conflict with the proposed improvements. Approved with conditions: 1. The existing water meter/s cannot be removed, and curb stops cannot be turned off before the Utilities Billing Office is contacted. The Utilities Billing Office is located at 1575 2nd Street Sarasota, FL 34236 with hours of operation from 8:00 A.M. to 4:30 P.M. Monday – Friday (excluding holidays and emergencies). Utilities Billing Office staff can be reached by calling 941-263-6260. 2. If the existing water meter is used as a construction/demo meter, a Reduced Pressure (RP) Backflow preventer must be installed prior to demolition and construction. A building inspector shall inspect the backflow and the backflow hanging tag. 3. If a backflow is installed, the property owner is required to provide a (RP) Backflow report/certification. The backflow test report shall be emailed to Backflow.utilities@sarasotafl.gov. 4. If a backflow is required and a backflow is not installed and a certificate (test report) is not provided, the Utilities Department will turn off the water. Billing Office fees will apply. 5. If water from the fire hydrant is used, an appropriate fee shall be paid directly to the Utilities Billing Office. 6. Call 811 for locates prior to beginning demolition. 7. The location of the existing wastewater lateral (sewer service line) shall be capped at the property line prior to demolition. The painted green wood stake shall be placed next to the capped pipe. Be advised that any Contractor that damages any portion of the City’s potable water, wastewater, and/or reclaimed water infrastructure shall be totally financially responsible for the repair of any such damaged infrastructure. All Contractors who propose to work directly on or in close proximity of any portion of the City’s potable water, wastewater, and/or reclaimed water infrastructure shall have the appropriate repair materials (pipe, fittings, etc.), tools, and qualified staff available onsite to perform immediate repairs should damage to such infrastructure occur.

Per Sec VII-312(e) Fences and walls shall not be installed where they interfere with the root system of existing trees. Post holes and trenches shall be adjusted to avoid damage to major roots. Post holes and trenches located close to trees shall be adjusted to avoid damage to major roots. Per Sec. VII-331.-Protection of tree roots. Arborist Conditions: Tree protection barriers shall be installed prior to the commencement of construction and shall remain in place until final building inspection. The City Arborist shall be notified prior to installation, and any modifications to tree protection barriers must be reviewed and approved by the City Arborist before changes are made. Section VII-312. (a)(f) The owner, builder, superintendent, contractor and site employees shall be responsible for the oversite of tree protection during all construction. A: Vertical wood members must be a minimum of 2” x 2” B: Vertical wood members must be a minimum of 3 feet from finished grade C: Vertical wood members may not exceed a distance greater than 8 feet D: Top wooden rails must be a minimum of 1” deep by 4” wide E: Distance from tree trunk to tree protection must be at least 10 feet For more information on tree protection, please see City of Sarasota Zoning Code, Section VII-312 Protection of trees during development, viewable online at www.Municode.com/Library/Fl/Sarasota/Codes/Zoning https://www.sarasotafl.gov/home/showdocument?id=10706 Utility Conditions: To the best of the Utilities Department’s knowledge, there does not appear to be any on-site City of Sarasota utilities in conflict with the proposed improvements. Approved with conditions: 1. The existing water meter/s cannot be removed, and curb stops cannot be turned off before the Utilities Billing Office is contacted. The Utilities Billing Office is located at 1575 2nd Street Sarasota, FL 34236 with hours of operation from 8:00 A.M. to 4:30 P.M. Monday – Friday (excluding holidays and emergencies). Utilities Billing Office staff can be reached by calling 941-263-6260. 2. If the existing water meter is used as a construction/demo meter, a Reduced Pressure (RP) Backflow preventer must be installed prior to demolition and construction. A building inspector shall inspect the backflow and the backflow hanging tag. 3. If a backflow is installed, the property owner is required to provide a (RP) Backflow report/certification. The backflow test report shall be emailed to Backflow.utilities@sarasotafl.gov. 4. If a backflow is required and a backflow is not installed and a certificate (test report) is not provided, the Utilities Department will turn off the water. Billing Office fees will apply. 5. If water from the fire hydrant is used, an appropriate fee shall be paid directly to the Utilities Billing Office. 6. Call 811 for locates prior to beginning demolition. 7. The location of the existing wastewater lateral (sewer service line) shall be capped at the property line prior to demolition. The painted green wood stake shall be placed next to the capped pipe. Be advised that any Contractor that damages any portion of the City’s potable water, wastewater, and/or reclaimed water infrastructure shall be totally financially responsible for the repair of any such damaged infrastructure. All Contractors who propose to work directly on or in close proximity of any portion of the City’s potable water, wastewater, and/or reclaimed water infrastructure shall have the appropriate repair materials (pipe, fittings, etc.), tools, and qualified staff available onsite to perform immediate repairs should damage to such infrastructure occur.

permits.description: Please note. There was no contractor involved. Apologies but We have done the work already not knowing a permit was needed. Applied for exemption which was denied. 1. Fence: We have an old chain link fence. We didn’t build a new fence. The property is surrounded on three sides by an old chain link fence. On the fourth side, there is a wooden fence but that’s not ours. 2. Wood Structure/Living Walls/Vertical Garden We like gardening and have been planting lots of plants to make the landscaping look nice and to create shade and privacy. The property sits on a corner lot with southwest exposure and has no privacy or shade without the plants. Neighbours always compliment us about how nice it looks. Some plants like jasmine have gotten so big that none of the trellises we could buy would support them so we built trellis/living wall that’s big enough for it to climb on. On the other side of it we put down pavers. Please note, we didn’t pour concrete or connected/grouted the pavers. They are just individual pavers so we can put down chairs/tables. other trellis/living wall is the same but we also screened it in because the mosquitoes are an issue and it also provides shade. We added a solar/plastic roof and we would like to add solar panels. We would also like to add a solar roof over the driveway. Please note, the solar/plastic roof is not connected to the main roof. We also screened in the carport. We just used the existing carport structure and added a screen around it and to make it look universal to the rest and to give support to the plants in front of it. Apologies but we didn’t realize we needed a permit for the above and hope we get to keep our beloved living walls and look forward to your approval
